title: NETRA analysis results
description: THE FROZEN CONTRACT. The single handshake between the ingestion/correlation layer, the ML core, the FastAPI backend and the NETRA dashboard. If a field changes here, the Captain announces it. Never edit silently.

entities.description: Every investigative subject: wallet clusters AND network endpoints (IPs). The dashboard graph is built from this list plus `edges`.

edges.description: Graph links. kind=flow is an on-chain value transfer; kind=control is a network-layer observation (IP controlled/relayed a wallet).

alerts.description: Ranked investigative leads, most severe first. This is the product - a lead list, not a verdict list.

geo_breakdown.description: Share of entity activity by country, descending. Powers the geo panel.

window.description: MONITORING ADDITION. Which time window this payload covers. Absent for a one-shot batch analysis, present for a windowed run -- so the dashboard always knows what 'now' means.

fleet.description: MONITORING ADDITION. Fleet-level counts for the baseline strip: is the FEED changing, not just the wallets in it.

events.description: MONITORING ADDITION. What changed since the previous window, with attribution. A score is a state; an event is a finding. Optional so a single-batch payload still validates.

traces.description: MONITORING ADDITION. Traced fund paths from a lead to the services it reached. An ESTIMATE, not a fact -- see the required `method` and `assumption` fields.

corpus.description: ANALYSIS OF THE ENTIRE INGESTED TRAFFIC. The problem statement asks to analyse Bitcoin transaction traffic; the suspicious subset is one OUTPUT of that analysis, not its frame. Every share in this block is a share of everything read.

behaviour.description: How the ingested traffic decomposes by observed behaviour, and how scores distribute across EVERY entity including the cleared ones -- so the dashboard can state what it examined, not only what it flagged.

total_value_btc.description: Sum of all output amounts across the ingested records -- the true total value moved. Reported so the dashboard never has to invent a headline figure.

flagged_entities.description: Entities at or above the medium risk band

id.description: E-#### for wallet clusters, N-#### for network endpoints. Four or more digits -- larger datasets produce 5-digit ids.

label.description: Short display label for the graph node

kind.description: Drives node colour/shape in the dashboard

role.description: One-sentence human explanation of what this node is

cluster.description: Cluster id this entity belongs to, or null

anomaly_score.description: Raw IsolationForest decision score (lower = more anomalous)

typology.description: Detected laundering typologies e.g. peel_chain, coinjoin_mixer, ransomware_fanin, cross_border_control

model.description: Which model produced the risk score

community_id.description: Graph community this entity belongs to, or null if it carries no material flow. NOT a verdict: weak community structure is a property of the data.

community_size.description: Size of that community, or 0 when the entity is in none. Never the size of the unassigned bucket -- 79 unrelated wallets are not an operation.

graph_role.description: Function within the flow graph. A heuristic label for the analyst's narrative, NOT a model input -- a rule-derived label fed to the model as a feature is how a rule quietly becomes the answer.

history.description: Risk across windows, oldest first. Powers the per-entity trend sparkline; an entity with no history has this empty rather than a fabricated flat line.

explanation.description: How the score decomposes. `base + contributions == prediction` up to `residual`, which is reported rather than assumed: a non-zero residual means the explanation does not reconcile with the score on screen.

method.description: e.g. 'exact TreeSHAP (XGBoost pred_contribs)' or 'exact decision-path contributions (Saabas), not Shapley'. Named because they are NOT equivalent and we do not call both SHAP.

residual.description: prediction - (base + sum of contributions). Should be ~0; reported so it can be checked.

features.description: Feature attributions for the explainability panel bars

importance.description: Signed contribution. Positive pushes toward illicit.

reasons.description: Plain-English justifications shown on every lead. This is what makes a lead defensible.

timeline.description: Ordered narrative of how the funds moved - shown in the case report

ref.description: txid or address anchoring this step

count.description: Number of transfers aggregated into this edge

entity.description: Entity id this lead points at; the graph selects this node

status.description: MONITORING ADDITION. The analyst's decision, remembered between runs. This is what separates a tool from a report.

first_window.description: Label of the window this lead first appeared in

last_window.description: Most recent window it was still above the floor. An alert that keeps updating is one alert, not one per run.

changes.description: MONITORING ADDITION: why this moved, ranked by change in robust z. 'Risk went up' is not actionable; 'risk 14 -> 55 because burst concentration 0.2 -> 0.5' is.

delta_z.description: Change measured in robust standard deviations (median/MAD), so one whale cannot make everything else look shifted.

hourly_volume.description: 3-hour buckets of traced BTC - the volume bar chart

risk_bands.description: Entity counts per band - the risk doughnut chart

code.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2; the dashboard derives the flag emoji from this

Metrics.description: Honest evaluation scores against the planted ground truth. Nulls are allowed and mean 'not yet measured' - never fake a number here.

cluster_ari.description: Adjusted Rand Index of clustering vs true_entity_id

brier.description: Calibration: is the score honest about its own confidence? 0 is perfect, 0.25 is what always answering 0.5 scores. Present because 'risk 92' should mean roughly 92%.

expected_calibration_error.description: Average gap between predicted probability and observed frequency across bins.

modularity.description: How clearly the wallet groups separate, 0 meaning no discernible pattern. Measured on the material-flow backbone, because small transfers connect unrelated wallets almost at random.

cv_folds.description: Cross-validation folds behind the metrics. A single split of a few hundred entities has too few positives to quote without a spread.

WindowInfo.description: Which slice of time this payload covers. Every number in a monitoring payload is window-scoped, so the window has to be on screen.

total.description: How many windows exist, so the UI can render '4 of 9' without a second request

Fleet.description: Counts about the FEED rather than the wallets in it, so an analyst can tell whether the data changed or the world did.

rows_rejected.description: Rejected by the data-quality gate. Silent data loss is indefensible, so the count is surfaced rather than swallowed.

Event.description: Something that CHANGED. A score is a state; a state that has not changed tells an analyst nothing new. Includes event types that can only exist across time (DORMANT, RESURGENT).

detail.description: The reason in plain language, built from the attribution

absorbed.description: CLUSTER_MERGE only: entity keys absorbed into this one. Two operations being linked is a finding, not bookkeeping.

changes.description: Attribution: which features moved, ranked by change in robust z

Trace.description: A traced fund path from a seed to the services it reached. ALWAYS an estimate: Bitcoin is fungible, so per-hop allocation is an allocation MODEL, not a fact. `method` and `assumption` are required so a traced figure can never be quoted without the model that produced it.

Corpus.description: Dataset-wide analysis of the traffic that was read. Exists so the tool reports the shape of EVERYTHING it ingested, with the flagged subset shown as a share of that whole rather than as the whole picture.

entities.description: Wallet groups in the whole capture

total_value_btc.description: Every output amount across the capture -- the denominator for every share

median_value_btc.description: Reported alongside the mean because Bitcoin values span nine orders of magnitude, where a mean describes nobody

value_percentiles.description: Distribution of transaction value. Percentiles, not a mean, because one whale would otherwise define the summary.

percentile.description: A number, not an integer: in heavy-tailed data the 99.9th percentile is where the interesting cases live, and rounding it to 100 would collapse the tail into the maximum.

size_classes.description: Transactions bucketed by value, so the SHAPE of ordinary traffic is visible and not only the extremes.

top_entities.description: The largest actors by value across the WHOLE capture. Most are lawful exchanges and payment processors, which is the point: the analysis covers everyone, not a curated list of suspects. `flagged` shows whether each also appears in the lead list.

countries.description: Countries observed across ALL traffic, with the flagged count inside each. The flagged column is a highlight, not the picture.

coverage.description: What the analysis covers, so that 'nothing found here' can be distinguished from 'not examined'.

Behaviour.description: How the ingested traffic decomposes, and how the scores distribute across every entity.

classes.description: A PARTITION of all wallet groups by observed behaviour: every group is counted exactly once, under the first class whose test it meets. The detectors overlap heavily (a mixer is usually also multi-country), so reporting them as independent flags would sum past 100% and mislead while looking fine.

label.description: Plain-language name, because the console is read by non-specialists too

explanation.description: How membership was determined, so a class is auditable rather than asserted

score_distribution.description: Every entity by priority band, including the cleared ones -- the statement that the whole corpus was scored, not only the suspects.

value_share_of_flagged.description: Share of all value moved that touches a flagged group. High means the capture's value sits with the leads; low means the leads are a thin slice of ordinary traffic.
